total_debt.note: Face value of long-term debt $127.485B at 2026-09-30 (vs $49.1B at 2025-12-31); carrying value net of current portion $125.1B. No commercial paper outstanding. Excludes ~C$6B notes priced 2026-11-19 and operating lease liabilities ($20.5B) / finance lease liabilities ($3.7B).

cash_and_marketable_securities.note: Cash & equivalents $56.3B + marketable securities $208.8B; boosted by 2026 debt and equity raises. Separately holds $135.2B of non-marketable securities (mostly private stakes incl. Anthropic, SpaceX).

free_cash_flow.note: First negative quarterly FCF; TTM FCF down ~73% (nextgcomm summary of slides). OCF also hit by TPU inventory build (inventory $13.3B vs $2.4B at YE2025).

shareholder_returns.note: No Class A/C repurchases in Q3 or 9M 2026 (vs $11.5B repurchased in Q3 2025). Instead sold $12.4B of stock via $40B ATM program in Q3; $27.6B ATM capacity left. Dividends still paid ($2.9B in Q3).

rpo_backlog.note: ~55% expected to be recognized within 24 months; includes $16.8B from related-party JV Crux AI.

q3_2026_income.note: Net income fell 24% YoY mainly on $8.7B loss on equity securities (SpaceX mark-down).

off_balance_items.description: Multi-year non-cancelable commitments for technical infrastructure & inventory, energy take-or-pay contracts and content licenses (remaining term >1 yr). Total material purchase commitments are $924.4B incl. open POs; $213.4B due within 12 months; significant majority fulfilled through 2031. Includes third-party compute capacity Google began renting late Q3.
off_balance_items.source_title: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Purchase Commitments / Note 10

off_balance_items.description: Future lease payments for leases signed but not yet commenced, primarily data centers and energy infrastructure; terms 1-26 years, commencing 2026-2031. Includes leases with data center leasing VIEs (finance leases).
off_balance_items.counterparty: Data center developers / energy infrastructure lessors

off_balance_items.description: Credit derivatives: Alphabet backstops third parties' data center lease payments and associated energy costs (e.g., Fluidstack leases at former crypto miners). Notional = maximum potential exposure on default; terms up to 15 years; fair value liability $606M. Google may assume the leases on default.
off_balance_items.counterparty: Data center lessees/landlords (incl. Fluidstack sites at TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8)

off_balance_items.description: Illustrative components of the data-center backstop book: Google backstops Fluidstack lease obligations at TeraWulf Lake Mariner (~$1.8B original + ~$1.3-1.4B for 168MW JV, ~$3.1-3.2B total; Google holds warrants for ~14% of TeraWulf) and at Cipher Mining Barber Lake (total $1.73B). Presumed included in the $48.0B notional above; not summed.
off_balance_items.source_title: TeraWulf & Cipher press releases; Startup Fortune

off_balance_items.description: Financial guarantees supporting counterparties' procurement of long-lead equipment for future power purchase / energy agreements; terms through Jan 2049.

TPU hardware repurchase guarantees: certain TPU system sale contracts require Google to buy back previously sold TPU hardware under specified conditions. Company says counterparties lack economic incentive to exercise.
off_balance_items.counterparty: TPU system buyers (undisclosed; likely AI labs/neoclouds)

off_balance_items.description: Crux AI JV with Blackstone (formed May 2026, announced Q3): Google committed to provide future data center and energy infrastructure backstops of up to $10.0B for agreements the venture enters into; Blackstone commits up to $5.0B of capital. Google holds minority equity-method stake (unconsolidated VIE). May partly overlap with credit-derivative notional once used; not summed.

Crux AI round trip: Google backstops the JV's data center agreements (up to $10B) AND the JV signed a multi-year commercial agreement to buy from Google, contributing $16.8B to Google's revenue backlog (related-party).

Equity investor in its own major cloud/TPU customer Anthropic: ~$33.3B invested to date (per Reuters calculation), ~13.4-14% stake (cap 14.99%) post-IPO; additionally committed $10B to Anthropic's concurrent private placement at the $83 IPO price (Nov 18, 2026). Stake worth roughly $139-147B at IPO price; large unrealized gains flow through Alphabet's income ($116B of 9M-2026 non-marketable gains).
off_balance_items.source_title: Bloomberg / Yahoo Finance on Anthropic S-1/A; SmartAsset IPO summary

off_balance_items.description: Anthropic's S-1 discloses at least $121.3B of non-cancelable compute commitments to Google (Apr 2026-Jul 2033, ~$16.7B/yr), ~21.6% of Google Cloud's $560.8B backlog (computed). Anthropic is itself vendor-financed (Google, Amazon, Nvidia, Microsoft investors; ~$900B total compute commitments). Earlier reporting (The Information, May 2026) put Anthropic's 5-yr Google spend at $200B, >40% of backlog then.
off_balance_items.source_title: GuruFocus via TradingView: Anthropic IPO filing shows $121.3B Google commitment

off_balance_items.description: Meta multi-year, multi-billion TPU rental deal with Google Cloud (Feb 2026); amount undisclosed. Adds another hyperscaler-scale AI customer to backlog.
off_balance_items.source_title: Reuters: Meta signs multi-billion-dollar deal to rent Google AI chips

off_balance_items.description: At-the-market equity program ($40B, June 2026) plus a separate ~$49.5B June stock sale: Alphabet is funding capex partly with new shares while buybacks are halted. $27.6B of ATM capacity remains.

total_note: Sum of hard, 10-Q-quantified items: purchase commitments >1yr $802.1B + leases not commenced $130.5B + data-center credit-derivative backstops $48.0B + energy financial guarantees $16.2B + TPU repurchase guarantees $6.6B = $1,003.4B. Excluded to avoid double counting or because not liabilities: Fluidstack/TeraWulf/Cipher backstops (inside the $48.0B), Crux AI $10B backstop commitment (may later appear in credit derivatives), $10B Anthropic private placement (cash outflow post-quarter, not an ongoing obligation), Anthropic $121.3B and Crux $16.8B (these are backlog/receivable-side concentration, not obligations), open POs ($122.3B within the $924.4B). Note most of the $802.1B is ordinary-course supply/energy purchases; the truly contingent 'hidden debt' (backstops + guarantees) is ~$71B, rising to ~$81B with Crux. Off-balance total ~5.6x TTM operating cash flow ($179.6B).

credit_signals.detail: Aa2, stable; assigned Aa2 to new senior unsecured notes on 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-12. In June 2026 Moody's called the $84.75B equity raise credit positive.
AA+, stable (affirmed on proposed notes; reiterated in Nov 2026 Canadian bond filing).

Q3 issuance net proceeds $28.7B: $23.8B USD fixed + $1.3B USD floating (WAC 5.55%, WAM 15 yrs) and A$5.6B AUD notes (WAC 5.82%). 2026 YTD: $45.0B USD + $35.8B foreign-currency senior notes; face debt rose from $49.1B to $127.5B.
C$6.0B in 3/8/12/40-yr tranches; 40-yr at 6.000% coupon. Spreads materially wider than May deal (12-yr +145bp vs 10-yr +75bp in May; 40-yr +185bp vs 30-yr +110bp).
$40B ATM program (June 2026): $12.4B sold in Q3 (12M Class A + 24M Class C shares). Plus ~$49.5B stock sale in June; Moody's referenced an $84.75B combined equity raise announcement on June 2.
Alphabet 2.25% 2060 bond quoted at ~6.14% yield (retail quote, date unverified).

news_context.headline_summary: Q3 2026: revenue $127.6B (+25%), first top-and-bottom-line miss in ~4 yrs; Cloud +103% to $30.7B; capex $51.4B, FCF -$9.1B; stock fell ~10%.
news_context.why_it_matters: First negative FCF quarter shows the buildout now outruns internal cash generation, so debt and equity issuance fill the gap.

news_context.headline_summary: CFO keeps 2026 capex at $195-205B and says 2027 capex will 'increase significantly'; Google began renting third-party compute late Q3 with margin headwinds.
news_context.why_it_matters: Spending is set to climb further, and renting third-party capacity adds more off-balance purchase commitments.

news_context.headline_summary: Anthropic IPO filing discloses $121.3B of compute commitments to Google through 2033; Google and Nvidia each to buy $10B of Anthropic stock in private placement.
news_context.why_it_matters: Google's single biggest backlog customer is one it funds; customer pays Google partly with Google's own investment dollars.

news_context.headline_summary: Anthropic prices IPO at $83/share (~$1.5T valuation); Google to own ~13.4-14% (cap 14.99%).
news_context.why_it_matters: Stake worth ~$140B+ inflates Alphabet's earnings via mark-to-market and makes Alphabet's results sensitive to Anthropic's stock price.

news_context.headline_summary: Alphabet prices C$6B bonds incl. 40-yr 6% note at noticeably wider spreads than its May deal.
news_context.why_it_matters: Even an AA+ borrower is paying more as AI-capex supply floods credit markets — an early credit-tightening signal.

news_context.headline_summary: 10-Q reveals $48.0B data-center credit-derivative backstops, $16.2B energy guarantees, $6.6B TPU repurchase guarantees and $130.5B of uncommenced leases.
news_context.why_it_matters: These contingent obligations are not debt on the balance sheet, so a ratio-based scorecard misses them.

news_context.headline_summary: Crux AI JV with Blackstone announced: Google backstops up to $10B and books $16.8B of related-party backlog from it.
news_context.why_it_matters: Classic circular structure: the supplier guarantees the customer's financing and counts the customer's purchases as backlog.

hidden_leverage_assessment.rationale: Alphabet still looks rock-solid on its own books (AA+/Aa2, $265B of cash and securities, ~$180B of yearly operating cash flow), but it is now acting as a lender and guarantor to the AI ecosystem. It backstops about $48B of other companies' data-center leases (including former bitcoin miners renting to Fluidstack), guarantees $16B of energy deals and $6.6B of TPU buybacks, and has $130B of data-center leases about to start plus ~$800B of multi-year purchase commitments. Its biggest cloud customer, Anthropic (~$121B of backlog), is partly financed by Alphabet's own equity checks, and the Crux AI JV is a round trip where Google guarantees a venture that buys from Google. Cash flow just turned negative, buybacks stopped and it is selling stock and long bonds at wider spreads, so it is no longer self-funding. Rating is Elevated rather than High because the core ads business throws off huge cash and the contingent pieces (~$71-81B) are under half a year of operating cash flow.
hidden_leverage_assessment.biggest_hidden_risk: If Anthropic or the neocloud tenants Google backstops (Fluidstack and crypto-miner landlords) hit a funding wall, Google simultaneously loses a fifth of its cloud backlog, takes write-downs on a ~$140B equity stake, and has to pay out on tens of billions of lease guarantees.
hidden_leverage_assessment.what_would_change_my_mind: A return to positive quarterly free cash flow while backstop notional shrinks and Anthropic's share of cloud backlog falls below ~10% would move this to Moderate.
